goal: Create an executable, dependency-ordered Nilaza MVP remediation roadmap, existing-agent ownership, future-task handoff backlog and manager acceptance gates without implementing application changes.
successCriteria: Every planned task has an existing owner role, dependencies, scope, validation, rollback and concrete manager acceptance.
Distinguish work that can start locally from dependency, environment, database, native-device and release gates.
Separate invited free beta, monetized MVP and store release; no unrun implementation or tests are labelled complete.
untouchedSurfaces: Application source, seed content, runtime prompts/routes, entitlements, RLS, schema and production are unchanged.
Existing audit evidence and canonical role/workflow configuration are preserved; no new persistent agents are registered.

impact.entryPoint: Planning document and task backlog consumed by the owner and delivery agents; app journeys are acceptance scenarios only.
impact.dataWrite: Only new planning Markdown and JSON files in the declared documentation scope; no app or database writes.
impact.backendContract: Future tasks explicitly name journal, entitlement, AI contracts, prompt versions and protected Admin boundaries; no API or schema is modified now.
impact.adminVisibility: Plan preserves Content Operations and AI Studio and distinguishes draft, active publication and genuine provider tests.
impact.privacySafety: Use only sanitized source context and fictional test scenarios; future auth/deletion and cost gates are recorded, no private rows or credentials accessed.
impact.observability: Task states remain planned or external-gated; future trace, release and measurement evidence must be attached before acceptance.
impact.rollback: Remove only new planning files if superseded; no runtime rollout or data rollback exists.

canonicalContracts: Existing coding-agents.json and feature-workflows.json define delivery-role IDs and lane ownership, not automatically running services.
Council and Astrology shared canonical contracts remain unchanged; future implementation requires task-specific refreshed preflight and contract validation.

skillReview.name: nilaza-plan-qc
skillReview.evidence: Applied complete impact map, dependency gates, existing roles and manager-testable acceptance; current guidance remains appropriate.

dependencyReview.evidence: This roadmap relies on current local docs/config and dated audit evidence. It selects no new dependency version, provider price or external API behavior; implementers must verify those before their own edits.

securityReview.authzRls: Plan only; future ownership, account isolation, entitlement and protected publisher tests are explicit release gates, not executed now.
securityReview.sensitiveData: No real user data or traces are loaded; subagents receive sanitized source context and fictional scenarios only.
securityReview.secretsLogging: No keys, environment values, login credentials or private outputs enter the roadmap or handoffs.
securityReview.externalInput: Treat audit observations as dated evidence, not mutation authority; future tasks rebaseline the reviewed source state.
securityReview.dependencies: No install/upgrade is performed; audit triage is a future ticket, not an automatic npm audit fix.
securityReview.migrationRelease: Ledger is blocked and future database writes require reconciliation and reviewed owner approval. This documentation record has no deployment, publication or database action.
securityReview.stopCondition: Stop planning scope expansion into implementation, live mutation, credentials, private data or release actions; create a separate reviewed task record before any code work.

workingTreeReview.note: This turn writes new documentation only and preserves the owner dirty working tree; current source hashes bind planning assumptions.

managerTestPath: Open the roadmap, inspect the milestone table, choose a task ID and review its exact handoff, start conditions and acceptance path in the backlog. Confirm no role is invented and no feature is marked implemented.
residualRisk: The 30 September audit is a dated baseline. Every implementation task must re-read its actual source, refresh preflight and prove runtime/native/backend evidence; this roadmap alone does not close MVP gaps.
